brief_item.title: VITAL-RAG按代码对象分配上下文证据
brief_item.core_conclusion: VITAL-RAG在检索与生成之间加入按代码对象分配证据的层，合并同一对象的多种视图，为每个对象保留一个相关伴随依赖，再在总预算内渲染上下文，缓解Read、Grep结果互相挤占。
brief_item.mechanism: 系统按规范化路径和标识符归并来源，为对象分配独立位置，并选择一个查询相关伴随项。评测使用总计4096 Token、单对象1024 Token上限和128 Token下限。
brief_item.result: RepoBench中，Recall@4K从39.59%升至63.67%，证据Token减少35.63%。RepoExec中，GPT-5.4、Claude Sonnet 4.6、Qwen3-8B的Pass@1分别为57.75%、65.63%和21.69%。
brief_item.boundary: 结果依赖固定候选组合、4096 Token预算和对象上限，其他上下文窗口需要重新调参。实验未覆盖更丰富的代码图或符号索引，跨仓库泛化仍待验证。
brief_item.project_relevance: 可同时记录检索入口与渲染后证据存活率，按语义对象去重并保留相关辅助对象，限制单对象Token占用，避免上下文构建阶段丢失证据。

facts.title: VITAL-RAG: Invariance Race for Context Allocation in Coding Agents
facts.event_hint: VITAL-RAG allocates bounded coding-agent context by canonical code object with one query-relevant companion
facts.problem: Repository retrieval can find relevant fragments yet lose them during bounded context construction: multiple views of one code object consume positions and token budget, crowding out distinct dependencies and helpers. Exact deduplication or coarse grouping can respectively miss semantic additions or discard local evidence.
facts.mechanism: VITAL-RAG inserts a provenance-aware allocation layer between retrieval and generation. It groups views by canonical code object and gives each one external position, reserves one slot for a distinct query-relevant companion from a selected provenance region, then renders selected objects under per-object and global token budgets (4K total, 1,024-token object cap in the evaluation).

evidence.claim: On RepoBench, VITAL-RAG increased Recall@4K from 39.59% to 63.67% while reducing evidence tokens by 35.63%.
evidence.baseline: Entity-First 4+1 baseline with fixed candidate portfolio
evidence.source_locator: PDF p.1 abstract; p.6 Table 3 and Section 6.2

evidence.claim: The pre-method RepoBench setting retrieved required evidence into the top five for 64.16% of tasks, but only 39.59% survived in the 4K model input.
On RepoExec's 355-task set, VITAL-RAG achieved the highest raw Pass@1 for all three backends: 57.75% Gpt-5.4, 65.63% Claude Sonnet 4.6, and 21.69% Qwen3-8B.
evidence.condition: one generation per task; repository tests determine Pass@1

evidence.claim: The evaluated allocation uses five slots, one query-relevant companion, a 4,096-token global budget, a 1,024-token per-object cap, and a 128-token minimum floor.
The 4+1 allocation improved strict recall over 5+0 on eligible RepoExec cases, while 3+2 added only a small strict-recall gain and reduced broad recall.
evidence.condition: 231-task ablation subset; query-relevant companion eligible in 33 cases

facts.evaluation_context: RepoBench uses 16,490 eligible tasks from 2,798 repositories with a fixed candidate portfolio and 4K evidence budget. Downstream evaluation uses RepoClassBench (227 tasks) and RepoExec (355 tasks) across Gpt-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Qwen3-8B, compared with CodeRAG, GraphCoder, and RepoScope-style allocations.
facts.limitations: The evaluated provenance adapter uses normalized paths and identifiers; richer graph or symbol indexes are not tested. Experiments use a fixed 4,096-token evidence budget and object caps, so other context windows require retuning. Optional program-semantic transfer is separate from context allocation and is precision-oriented; broad generalization beyond the tested repository benchmarks is not established.
facts.project_relevance: VITAL-RAG directly targets the Read/Grep/context-construction bottleneck: deduplicate by semantic object, preserve one distinct local helper when query-relevant, and cap each object's token authority. This suggests measuring both retrieval entry and post-render evidence survival instead of optimizing search recall alone.
source_notes: The arXiv v1 PDF and both referenced chunks were fetched; evidence locators refer to PDF pages and sections.
Reported metrics retain their benchmark, baseline, and budget conditions.
